clue.text: Find views of university in excellent books

parts.note: sound means excellent or in good condition

indicators.note: in says the university letter sits inside the abbreviation for books

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a university's opinions in some first-rate volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find views' is the definition as a whole phrase: to sound out is to probe opinions. 'in' puts U inside OT.
explanation.definitionFit: To sound out people is to discover their views by questioning them, so the phrase covers the whole definition idea of finding views.

clue.text: Opening for Steptoe's rubbish? Plenty here

definitions.text: Opening for Steptoe's rubbish? Plenty here

indicators.note: opening for means the first letter of the name Steptoe

parts.note: crap is slang for rubbish
heaps means plenty

explanation.surface: A junk dealer's first loads of junk are piled high here.
explanation.walkthrough: Steptoe and Son was a British sitcom about rag-and-bone men, scrap dealers, so the whole clue describes where they find their rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapheaps are piles of discarded junk, the source of a scrap dealer's goods.

clue.text: It may be stuffed poultry he's cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are prepared and changed, rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird for the oven can be stuffed, prepared by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed' and 'poultry' together suggest a turkey; the stuffing is really sofa padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Upholstery is the padded covering of furniture, filled with stuffing.

clue.text: President unknown in Middle East state? Not entirely

indicators.note: in places the unknown inside the shortened state
not entirely means the final letter is left off

parts.note: Dubai is an emirate in the Gulf
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An anonymous head of state in the Gulf is only partly identified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' trims DUBAI to DUBA; 'in' puts Y inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubya, a Texan rendering of W, was a nickname for US President George W. Bush.

clue.text: Fully functional as a mountain stream

definitions.meaning: a stream high up in the hills is up, and it is running water

explanation.definitionFit: A working system is up and running; a hill brook is literally up high and flowing.

clue.text: Wretched sailor getting cold in stream

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor

indicators.note: in tells us the cold letter goes inside the word for stream

parts.note: a jet is a stream of liquid or gas
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A miserable seaman feels the chill while standing in running water.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject describes a state of utter misery or degradation, a synonym of wretched.

clue.text: Egg roll for starters in old-fashioned club or restaurant

indicators.note: in puts those letters inside the club

parts.note: a brassie is an old name for a golf club, the number two wood

indicators.note: for starters means take the first letters of egg and roll

explanation.surface: An egg roll is served as an appetiser in a traditional club or eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: A brassie is an obsolete golf club; 'Egg roll' looks like food but gives just ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style eating place serving simple meals.

clue.text: Outer Mongolia supports Forster novel

indicators.note: supports in a down clue means the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: E. M. Forster, the English novelist, gives his initials

indicators.note: outer means the first and last letters of Mongolia

explanation.surface: A distant land underpins a book by a famous English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forster novel' suggests one of his books, but Forster is EM and 'novel' alone defines Jane Austen's book.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen, published in 1815.

clue.text: Brown bears right in lake

indicators.note: bears means carries, so the colour holds the right letter

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Brown bears are found in the right lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown bears' reads as the animals; 'bears' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, especially in the north of England.

clue.text: Extremely rude vagrant came inside for wine bottle

indicators.note: extremely here means take the extreme letters, the first and last, of the word rude

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp or vagrant

indicators.note: inside says to take only the letters within the word came, losing its ends

explanation.surface: A coarse tramp turned up indoors looking for a big bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' and 'inside' are opposite selections: one keeps the ends of a word, the other throws them away.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehoboam is a large wine or champagne bottle holding six standard bottles, named after a biblical king.

clue.text: Conjuror sometimes a pilgrim

definitions.meaning: a conjuror who palms cards or coins, hiding them in the hand, is one who palms
a medieval pilgrim back from the Holy Land carried a palm leaf as a sign of the journey

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a playful coinage: a magician who palms things is, literally, one who palms.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from palm: a sleight-of-hand performer palms objects, and a crusading pilgrim bore a palm frond home.

clue.text: Action! Send on cast for film!

indicators.note: cast means thrown about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A director calls action and sends the cast on for the film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie in the surface but means a thin coating, as of moisture.
explanation.definitionFit: Condensation forms a thin film of water droplets on a cold surface.

clue.text: Heartless girl close to tears after playing around with more than one husband

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the girl's name is removed

parts.note: Polly is a girl's name

indicators.note: playing here means the word around is rearranged, as if played about with
close to means the final letter of the word tears

explanation.surface: A girl with no heart ends up in tears after fooling around with several husbands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' drops the middle letter of the girl; 'playing' rearranges the word around; 'close to' takes the last letter of tears; 'after' puts that rearrangement behind the girl's piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyandry is the practice of a woman having several husbands at once, so a polyandrous woman has more than one.

clue.text: Ship — Titanic — one going down in salt water

indicators.note: in puts the reworked word inside the salt water

parts.note: brine is salt water

indicators.note: going down in a down clue means the one letter shifts lower, later in the word

parts.note: titanic means huge, as is giant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The famous liner sinks into the sea with everyone aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titanic' is not the liner but an adjective meaning huge; 'going down' slides its one letter lower in the word before it goes 'in' the salt water.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigantine is a two-masted sailing vessel, a type of ship.

clue.text: One has twelve houses, making realtors go crazy

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Owning a dozen homes would drive estate agents wild.
explanation.walkthrough: The twelve houses are the divisions of the zodiac chart in astrology, not property.
explanation.definitionFit: A horoscope caster divides the sky into twelve houses, so such a person works with twelve of them.

clue.text: Log first axed in middle of America

indicators.note: first axed means the opening letter is chopped off

parts.note: the American spelling of centre, the middle, is center

explanation.surface: A tree is felled first in the American heartland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of America' does double duty: it is the US spelling, CENTER, that we need before 'first axed' removes its C.
explanation.definitionFit: To log an item is to record it, which is to enter it in a register or book.

clue.text: In Hollywood Claude shed tears, often getting soaked

parts.note: Claude Rains was a Hollywood actor, star of Casablanca
to shed tears is to weep, past tense wept

explanation.surface: A film star in Hollywood cried and got drenched.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainswept place is frequently lashed by rain, so it is regularly drenched.

clue.text: Prepared for conflict in pits?

definitions.meaning: armpits are the underarm areas of the body

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers under arms are equipped for battle, and armpits, the pits, are also called the underarms.

clue.text: Gluttons' bread ration somewhere in France

parts.note: per as in an allowance per person, a share for each
a pig is a glutton
naan or nan is a flat Indian bread

explanation.surface: Greedy eaters get an allowance of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the pieces as 'per pig, nan': a nan bread for each glutton, a bread ration.
explanation.definitionFit: Perpignan is a city in southern France, near the Spanish border, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Crime writer Wallace and Gromit initially read in translation

indicators.note: in translation means the letters are rendered into a different form, rearranged
initially means take the first letter of Gromit

explanation.surface: Fans of the animated duo Wallace and Gromit read a crime author in a foreign edition.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallace and Gromit are a British plasticine-animation inventor and dog; here Wallace belongs to the definition, Edgar Wallace, the thriller writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Wallace was a prolific British thriller author best known for creating King Kong's story.

clue.text: Staggering behind empty stable, second in horse race

indicators.note: behind places the race piece after the emptied stable
empty means the inside of the word stable is cleared out, leaving its ends
in puts the second letter inside the race

parts.note: the Grand National is Britain's most famous steeplechase, often called the National

explanation.surface: A horse lurches out from behind an empty stable, in second place in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is a famous British steeplechase at Aintree. 'empty' leaves SE from 'stable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggering, as in astonishing, is a synonym of sensational.

clue.text: Sound of sleigh bells? Non-starter in a hot spot

indicators.note: non-starter means the first letter is removed

parts.note: sleigh bells jingle, and their sound is a jingle

explanation.surface: No sleigh bells ringing in a warm corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of' looks like a homophone signal but is part of the description of a jingle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a domestic fire or fireplace, the warm spot of a room.

clue.text: Not all classical music is serene

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Classical music is soothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'is serene' cannot swap for an adjective; 'is' is a link word, and 'serene' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and serene are synonyms for peaceful and untroubled.

clue.text: Girl lacking energy, needing good psychiatrist

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the energy letter is dropped

parts.note: June is a girl's name
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A listless girl needs a good therapist.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Jung was the Swiss founder of analytical psychology, a famous psychiatrist.

clue.text: A daughter of Mnemosyne — daughter unlike Queen Victoria

parts.note: the nine Muses were the daughters of Mnemosyne, goddess of memory

explanation.surface: A goddess's daughter is unlike a famously stern queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is famously credited with saying 'We are not amused'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quip 'We are not amused' is attributed to Victoria, so being entertained is the opposite of her.

clue.text: What a canary will do repeatedly in prison

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word is given twice

parts.note: a canary sings

explanation.surface: A songbird keeps on singing in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sing' is also slang for informing to the police, which suits a prison picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Sing Sing is a well-known maximum-security penitentiary in New York State.

clue.text: Very smooth malt whisky finally put on plane

indicators.note: put on means the final letters are added after the plane

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft

indicators.note: finally takes the last letters of smooth, malt and whisky

explanation.surface: A mellow single malt is served on a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' covers all three words, giving H, T and Y; 'Very smooth' looks like one phrase but 'Very' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty is informal, chiefly American, for very, as in mighty fine.

clue.text: Organ part that is holding notes back

indicators.note: holding means the abbreviation for that is contains the notes

parts.note: ie, id est, is the abbreviation for that is
N is an abbreviation for note, so two notes give two Ns
the rear is the back

explanation.surface: A section of a church organ is keeping some music in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a reversal signal but is just REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner ear is the deepest part of the hearing organ, holding the cochlea.
